summary: The sprint delivers a unified payment administration workspace for Treasury Operations, replacing fragmented spreadsheets with a secure, high-performance platform that integrates PaymentCore and Payment Rail data. Analysts and managers gain controlled access to search merchants and batches, drill into settlements, trigger refunds, approve payouts, and generate audit-ready reports, ensuring compliance and operational efficiency across regions.
scope_overview: This release includes the production-ready MVP of the payment admin workspace built with Next.js 14 and TypeScript. Core features: merchant/batch search, settlement drill-down, refund initiation, payout approvals with automated allocation, anomaly alerts, and audit report exports. All actions are logged to Kafka and archived in S3 with RBAC enforcement and integration with PaymentCore (GraphQL) and Payment Rail (REST) APIs via secured API Gateway.
key_risks: API latency from PaymentCore or Payment Rail may breach SLA thresholds (<1.5s for search, <4s for payouts).
RBAC misconfiguration could expose sensitive approval workflows to unauthorized users.
test_readiness: QA reports strong test coverage across search, refund, approval, and export workflows with E2E and integration tests validating performance and RBAC compliance. Kafka/S3 audit emissions are verified, and all high-priority test cases pass functional and security criteria. System is test-ready for production deployment under defined SLAs.
recommendations: Monitor live API latency and implement caching to mitigate performance risks during peak transaction volumes.
Conduct UAT with Treasury Ops managers to confirm approval and audit workflows before release sign-off.
next_steps: Finalize deployment within private VNet, enforcing mTLS and OAuth2 configurations.
Schedule business rollout and training sessions for 60 regional analysts and managers post-production release.
